reported.experiments_note: reported = PR body (us, median of the author's benchmark on their GPU)

gap.verdict:
contention / WSL2 host overhead** (not hardware)
Reported median 59.89→39.65 µs (author's runs 59.4-60.2, 39.5-39.7: sd < 1 %). Ours
106→78.5 µs with sd 23 / 16 µs (22 %). Per-run medians are **bimodal**: baseline
[89, 107, 91, 72, 132], PR's solution [71, 72, 71, 131, 88] — both arms touch ~71 and ~131 µs, a 1.85×
step. The benchmark is wall-clock around 4000 calls that each `.tolist()`/sync, so it measures
host launch+sync latency, not GPU work. Our *floor* (71 µs) is identical for baseline and PR's solution: the
PR's saving (fewer GPU bytes) is entirely hidden under WSL2 launch/sync latency, and the 1.35×
"gain" we record is an artefact of which runs landed on the slow mode. Verdict: box, not GPU —
P/E-core placement of the WSL2 vCPU and/or other tenants. Bench script is the author's verbatim
(64 × 128 tokens, subgroup 32, hidden 4096, bf16, 500 warmup, 5 × 4000). Fix: recommendations
1-5; also run baseline / PR-solution interleaved (ABBA) so both arms sample the same mode.

### 33538 — Triton top-k/top-p sampler vs PyTorch sort — **WSL2 launch latency (box), small-batch rows
gap.note: Baseline arm cannot run the script (it is introduced by the PR); baseline = the script's own "PyTorch (ms)" column in the PR's-solution run (by design, `task.json:workload.base_note`). Reported PyTorch 0.28 ms at b16 v32k; ours 1.21 ms. Our PyTorch column is **flat in batch**: 1.14 ms at b128, 1.23 ms at b16, 0.23-0.28 ms at b1 — i.e. ~1.1 ms of fixed per-call overhead for the ~20-30 kernels the sort/cumsum/mask path launches, vs the author's floor of ~0.10 ms (their b1 row). That is a 10× per-launch gap, exactly the WSL2 signature. The Triton arm (3-4 launches) is only 1.6× off the author (0.067 → 0.109 ms), so our 11× ratio vs their 4.2× overstates the PR at small batch. Large-batch rows (b2048: 20.4 / 81.5 ms PyTorch) are bandwidth-bound and are the honest comparison. Args are a superset of the author's (`--batch-sizes 1 16 128 2048`; author also ran 4 24 32 48 56). Cannot be made 1:1 on WSL2; report b2048 rows as headline or note the floor.
